spatial_and_orientation_analysis: The reference and delivered image both show a central two-pane window above rows of dark desks and white wheeled chairs, with two lamps at the right; visually the candidate is more frontal and distant, has a smaller window and furniture, a large empty foreground and less pronounced rightward depth convergence. Evidence: supplied reference and candidate images; build.py:57-100.

The reference foreground chairs overlap desks and show varied apparent facing, especially at right; candidate chair backs are similarly oriented toward the camera with small randomized yaw, and its more regular two-row arrangement changes occlusion. Evidence: supplied images; build.py:63-88.

Camera, room geometry, object positions and scale interact, so these 2D differences do not isolate a single 3D cause. No aligned coordinate frame or reliable world-space position/angle error is established. Evidence: build.py:21-26,57-60,88,99-100; input_index.json:33.
appearance_and_resource_analysis: Reference has pale hexagonal walls and warm lamp pools; the candidate retains the pattern and lamps but appears grayer and flatter, with weaker, less directional pools. Evidence: supplied reference and candidate images; build.py:27-50,89-98.

build.py:6-8 sets flat base color, roughness and metallic on Principled BSDF materials. The default Principled-to-material-output path is used; there is no authored image-texture, texture-coordinate, Mapping, Noise or ramp network in this material function. Hexagons are separate beveled poly curves bound to 'fine hexagon lines', not a texture mapping; see build.py:27-50 and original object_inventory.jsonl:2-7. Thus image path, packing and mapping direction/scale are not applicable to this pattern. original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:3-7 reports no missing external images.

The panes are opaque pale-blue Principled surfaces rather than a modeled wall opening: 'back wall', 'window recess', 'left window pane' and 'right window pane' are separately constructed cubes, build.py:23,51-56 and object_inventory.jsonl:2,8-10. No full-reference image plane is indicated by the executed source or original inventory.
geometry_analysis: Eight desk tops each use four thin rods, and eight chairs use a seat ellipsoid, a subdivided solidified back, post, five spokes and ellipsoid caster approximations; build.py:57-88 and original object_inventory.jsonl:16-159. These are editable discrete components, not proof of connected or mechanically functional assemblies.

The floor top is z=0 while desk leg rods begin at z=0.04, so their designed lower ends sit above the floor; build.py:22,62. For instance original object_inventory.jsonl:17 records a leg lower bound approximately 0.04. No full support or penetration test is claimed.

Lamp round base is centered at z=0.025 with depth 0.025, leaving its lower face at z=0.0125 above the floor top; build.py:22,92 and original object_inventory.jsonl:161,166. This is a geometric gap, not a verified physics outcome.
The reference's far-right cabinet sliver has a visible GT instance 125, reference_instance_statistics.json:482-495, but no cabinet is created in build.py:1-104.
